    77→def _scorecard_subjective(
    78→    state: dict,
    79→    dim_scores: dict,
    80→) -> list[dict]:
    81→    """Return scorecard-aligned subjective entries for current dimension scores."""
    82→    return _scorecard_subjective_impl(state, dim_scores)
    83→
    84→
    85→def _low_subjective_dimensions(
    86→    state: dict,
    87→    dim_scores: dict,
    88→    *,
    89→    threshold: float = DEFAULT_TARGET_STRICT_SCORE,
    90→) -> list[tuple[str, float, int]]:
    91→    """Return assessed scorecard-subjective entries below the threshold."""
    92→    low: list[tuple[str, float, int]] = []
    93→    for entry in _scorecard_subjective(state, dim_scores):
    94→        if entry.get("placeholder"):
    95→            continue
    96→        strict_val = float(entry.get("strict", entry.get("score", 100.0)))
    97→        if strict_val < threshold:
    98→            low.append(
    99→                (
   100→                    str(entry.get("name", "Subjective")),
   101→                    strict_val,
   102→                    int(entry.get("failing", 0)),
   103→                )
   104→            )
   105→    low.sort(key=lambda item: item[1])
   106→    return low
   107→
   108→
   109→def cmd_next(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   110→    """Show next highest-priority queue items."""
   111→    runtime = command_runtime(args)
   112→    state = runtime.state
   113→    config = runtime.config
   114→    if not require_completed_scan(state):
   115→        return
   116→
   117→    skill_warning = check_skill_version()
   118→    if skill_warning:
   119→        print(colorize(f"  {skill_warning}", "yellow"))
   120→    config_warning = check_config_staleness(config)
   121→    if config_warning:
   122→        print(colorize(f"  {config_warning}", "yellow"))
   123→
   124→    print_triage_guardrail_info(state=state)
   125→    _build_and_render_queue(args, state, config)
   126→
   127→
   128→def _resolve_cluster_focus(
   129→    plan_data: dict | None,
   130→    *,
   131→    cluster_arg: str | None,
   132→    scope: str | None,
   133→) -> str | None:
   134→    effective_cluster = cluster_arg
   135→    if plan_data and not cluster_arg and not scope:
   136→        active_cluster = plan_data.get("active_cluster")
   137→        if active_cluster:
   138→            effective_cluster = active_cluster
   139→    return effective_cluster
   140→
   141→
   142→def _build_next_payload(
   143→    *,
   144→    queue: dict,
   145→    items: list[dict],
   146→    state: dict,
   147→    narrative: dict,
   148→    plan_data: dict | None,
   149→) -> dict:
   150→    payload = next_output_mod.build_query_payload(
   151→        queue, items, command="next", narrative=narrative, plan=plan_data
   152→    )
   153→    scores = state_mod.score_snapshot(state)
   154→    payload["overall_score"] = scores.overall
   155→    payload["objective_score"] = scores.objective
   156→    payload["strict_score"] = scores.strict
   157→    payload["scorecard_dimensions"] = scorecard_dimensions_payload(
   158→        state,
   159→        dim_scores=state.get("dimension_scores", {}),
   160→    )
   161→    payload["subjective_measures"] = [
   162→        row for row in payload["scorecard_dimensions"] if row.get("subjective")
   163→    ]
   164→    return payload
   165→
   166→
   167→def _emit_requested_output(
   168→    opts: NextOptions,
   169→    payload: dict,
   170→    items: list[dict],
   171→) -> bool:
   172→    if opts.output_file:
   173→        if next_output_mod.write_output_file(
   174→            opts.output_file,
   175→            payload,
   176→            len(items),
   177→            safe_write_text_fn=safe_write_text,
   178→            colorize_fn=colorize,
   179→        ):
   180→            return True
   181→        raise CommandError("Failed to write output file")
   182→
   183→    if next_output_mod.emit_non_terminal_output(opts.output_format, payload, items):
   184→        return True
   185→    return False
   186→
   187→
   188→def _plan_queue_context(
   189→    *,
   190→    state: dict,
   191→    plan_data: dict | None,
   192→    context=None,
   193→) -> tuple[float | None, QueueBreakdown | None]:
   194→    effective_plan = context.plan if context is not None else plan_data
   195→    plan_start_strict = get_plan_start_strict(effective_plan)
   196→    try:
   197→        breakdown = plan_aware_queue_breakdown(state, plan_data, context=context)
   198→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS:
   199→        breakdown = None
   200→    return plan_start_strict, breakdown
   201→
   202→
   203→def _merge_potentials_safe(raw_potentials: dict | None) -> dict | None:
   204→    try:
   205→        return merge_potentials(raw_potentials) or None
   206→    except (ImportError, TypeError, ValueError):
   207→        return raw_potentials or None
   208→
   209→
   210→def _build_and_render_queue(args: argparse.Namespace, state: dict, config: dict) -> None:
   211→    opts = NextOptions.from_args(args)
   212→
   213→    target_strict = target_strict_score_from_config(config)
   214→
   215→    # Load the living plan
   216→    plan = load_plan()
   217→    plan_data: dict | None = None
   218→    if (
   219→        plan.get("queue_order")
   220→        or plan.get("overrides")
   221→        or plan.get("clusters")
   222→    ):
   223→        plan_data = plan
   224→
   225→    # Build unified context once — all downstream consumers agree on
   226→    # plan, target_strict, and subjective visibility policy.
   227→    ctx = queue_context(
   228→        state, config=config, plan=plan_data, target_strict=target_strict,
   229→    )
   230→
   231→    # Auto-scope to focus cluster if set and no explicit scope/cluster
   232→    effective_cluster = _resolve_cluster_focus(
   233→        plan_data,
   234→        cluster_arg=opts.cluster,
   235→        scope=opts.scope,
   236→    )
   237→
   238→    queue = build_work_queue(
   239→        state,
   240→        options=QueueBuildOptions(
   241→            count=None,
   242→            scope=opts.scope,
   243→            status=opts.status,
   244→            include_subjective=True,
   245→            subjective_threshold=target_strict,
   246→            explain=opts.explain,
   247→            include_skipped=opts.include_skipped,
   248→            cluster=effective_cluster,
   249→            context=ctx,
   250→        ),
   251→    )
   252→    items = queue.get("items", [])
   253→
   254→    # Collapse auto-clusters into display meta-items
   255→    if plan_data and not effective_cluster and not plan_data.get("active_cluster"):
   256→        items = collapse_clusters(items, plan_data)
   257→
   258→    # Apply count truncation after collapsing
   259→    if opts.count:
   260→        items = items[: opts.count]
   261→        queue["items"] = items
   262→        queue["total"] = len(items)
   263→
   264→    lang = resolve_lang(args)
   265→    lang_name = lang.name if lang else None
   266→    narrative = compute_narrative(
   267→        state,
   268→        context=NarrativeContext(lang=lang_name, command="next", plan=plan_data),
   269→    )
   270→
   271→    payload = _build_next_payload(
   272→        queue=queue,
   273→        items=items,
   274→        state=state,
   275→        narrative=narrative,
   276→        plan_data=plan_data,
   277→    )
   278→    write_query(payload)
   279→
   280→    if _emit_requested_output(opts, payload, items):
   281→        return
   282→
   283→    dim_scores = state.get("dimension_scores", {})
   284→    issues_scoped = state_mod.path_scoped_issues(
   285→        state.get("issues", {}),
   286→        state.get("scan_path"),
   287→    )
   288→
   289→    # Extract frozen plan-start score and queue breakdown for lifecycle display
   290→    plan_start_strict, breakdown = _plan_queue_context(
   291→        state=state,
   292→        plan_data=plan_data,
   293→        context=ctx,
   294→    )
   295→    queue_total = breakdown.queue_total if breakdown else 0
   296→
   297→    _render_queue_header(queue, opts.explain)
   298→    strict_score = state_mod.score_snapshot(state).strict
   299→    if _show_empty_queue(
   300→        queue,
   301→        strict_score,
   302→        plan_start_strict=plan_start_strict,
   303→        target_strict=target_strict,
   304→    ):
   305→        return
   306→
   307→    raw_potentials = state.get("potentials", {})
   308→    potentials = _merge_potentials_safe(raw_potentials)
   309→    next_render_mod.render_terminal_items(
   310→        items, dim_scores, issues_scoped, group=opts.group, explain=opts.explain,
   311→        potentials=potentials, plan=plan_data,
   312→        cluster_filter=effective_cluster,
   313→    )
   314→    next_nudges_mod.render_single_item_resolution_hint(items)
   315→    next_nudges_mod.render_uncommitted_reminder(plan_data)
   316→    next_nudges_mod.render_followup_nudges(
   317→        state,
   318→        dim_scores,
   319→        issues_scoped,
   320→        strict_score=strict_score,
   321→        target_strict_score=target_strict,
   322→        queue_total=queue_total,
   323→        plan_start_strict=plan_start_strict,
   324→        breakdown=breakdown,
   325→    )
   326→    print()
   327→
   328→    if items and plan_data:
   329→        print_user_message(
   330→            "Hey — the task details are printed above. Just start"
   331→            " working on it. When you're done, resolve it with"
   332→            " `desloppify plan resolve` and then run `desloppify"
   333→            " next` again. If this doesn't seem like the right"
   334→            " priority, run `desloppify plan show` to see the full"
   335→            " queue, or `desloppify plan --help` for all plan tools."
   336→            " Don't stop until you're done — unless I've told you"
   337→            " otherwise, just keep going."
   338→        )
   339→

    17→
    18→@dataclass
    19→class TriageGuardrailResult:
    20→    """Structured result from triage staleness detection."""
    21→
    22→    is_stale: bool = False
    23→    new_ids: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
    24→    _plan: dict | None = field(default=None, repr=False)
    25→
    26→
    27→def triage_guardrail_status(
    28→    *,
    29→    plan: dict | None = None,
    30→    state: dict | None = None,
    31→) -> TriageGuardrailResult:
    32→    """Pure detection: is triage stale? Returns structured result, no side effects."""
    33→    try:
    34→        resolved_plan = plan if isinstance(plan, dict) else load_plan()
    35→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS:
    36→        return TriageGuardrailResult()
    37→
    38→    resolved_state = state or {}
    39→
    40→    if not is_triage_stale(resolved_plan, resolved_state):
    41→        return TriageGuardrailResult(_plan=resolved_plan)
    42→
    43→    new_ids: set[str] = set()
    44→    if resolved_state:
    45→        new_ids = compute_new_issue_ids(resolved_plan, resolved_state)
    46→
    47→    return TriageGuardrailResult(is_stale=True, new_ids=new_ids, _plan=resolved_plan)
    48→
    49→
    50→def print_triage_guardrail_info(
    51→    *,
    52→    plan: dict | None = None,
    53→    state: dict | None = None,
    54→) -> bool:
    55→    """Print yellow info banner if triage is stale. Returns True if banner was shown."""
    56→    result = triage_guardrail_status(plan=plan, state=state)
    57→    if not result.is_stale:
    58→        return False
    59→
    60→    if result.new_ids:
    61→        print(colorize(
    62→            f"  {len(result.new_ids)} new review issue(s) not yet triaged.",
    63→            "yellow",
    64→        ))
    65→
    66→    if result._plan is not None:
    67→        banner = triage_phase_banner(result._plan)
    68→        if banner:
    69→            print(colorize(f"  {banner}", "yellow"))
    70→
    71→    return True
    72→
    73→
    74→def require_triage_current_or_exit(
    75→    *,
    76→    state: dict,
    77→    bypass: bool = False,
    78→    attest: str = "",
    79→) -> None:
    80→    """Gate: exit(1) if triage is stale and not bypassed. Name signals the exit."""
    81→    result = triage_guardrail_status(state=state)
    82→    if not result.is_stale:
    83→        return
    84→
    85→    if bypass and attest and len(attest.strip()) >= 30:
    86→        print(colorize(
    87→            "  Triage guardrail bypassed with attestation.",
    88→            "yellow",
    89→        ))
    90→        return
    91→
    92→    new_ids = result.new_ids
    93→    lines = [
    94→        f"BLOCKED: {len(new_ids) or 'some'} new review issue(s) have not been triaged."
    95→    ]
    96→    if new_ids:
    97→        for fid in sorted(new_ids)[:5]:
    98→            f = state.get("issues", {}).get(fid, {})
    99→            lines.append(f"    * [{short_issue_id(fid)}] {f.get('summary', '')}")
   100→        if len(new_ids) > 5:
   101→            lines.append(f"    ... and {len(new_ids) - 5} more")
   102→    lines.append("")
   103→    lines.append("  NEXT STEP: desloppify plan triage")
   104→    lines.append("  (Review new issues, then either --confirm-existing or re-plan.)")
   105→    lines.append("")
   106→    lines.append("  View new items:  desloppify plan queue --sort recent")
   107→    lines.append('  To bypass: --force-resolve --attest "I understand the plan may be stale..."')
   108→    raise CommandError("\n".join(lines))

   113→        _restore_file_snapshot(effective_state_path, state_snapshot)
   114→        _restore_file_snapshot(effective_plan_path, plan_snapshot)
   115→        raise

   168→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   169→# Skip / unskip
   170→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   171→
   172→
   173→def _validate_skip_requirements(
   174→    *,
   175→    kind: str,
   176→    attestation: str | None,
   177→    note: str | None,
   178→) -> bool:
   179→    if not skip_kind_requires_attestation(kind):
   180→        return True
   181→    if not validate_attestation(attestation):
   182→        show_attestation_requirement(
   183→            "Permanent skip" if kind == "permanent" else "False positive",
   184→            attestation,
   185→            ATTEST_EXAMPLE,
   186→        )
   187→        return False
   188→    if skip_kind_requires_note(kind) and not note:
   189→        print(
   190→            colorize("  --permanent requires --note to explain the decision.", "yellow"),
   191→            file=sys.stderr,
   192→        )
   193→        return False
   194→    return True
   195→
   196→
   197→def _apply_state_skip_resolution(
   198→    *,
   199→    kind: str,
   200→    state_file: Path | None,
   201→    issue_ids: list[str],
   202→    note: str | None,
   203→    attestation: str | None,
   204→) -> dict | None:
   205→    status = skip_kind_state_status(kind)
   206→    if status is None:
   207→        return None
   208→    state_data = state_mod.load_state(state_file)
   209→    for fid in issue_ids:
   210→        state_mod.resolve_issues(
   211→            state_data,
   212→            fid,
   213→            status,
   214→            note or "",
   215→            attestation=attestation,
   216→        )
   217→    return state_data
   218→
   219→
   220→def cmd_plan_skip(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   221→    """Skip issues — unified command for temporary/permanent/false-positive."""
   222→    runtime = command_runtime(args)
   223→    state = runtime.state
   224→    if not require_completed_scan(state):
   225→        return
   226→
   227→    patterns: list[str] = getattr(args, "patterns", [])
   228→    reason: str | None = getattr(args, "reason", None)
   229→    review_after: int | None = getattr(args, "review_after", None)
   230→    permanent: bool = getattr(args, "permanent", False)
   231→    false_positive: bool = getattr(args, "false_positive", False)
   232→    note: str | None = getattr(args, "note", None)
   233→    attestation: str | None = getattr(args, "attest", None)
   234→
   235→    kind = skip_kind_from_flags(permanent=permanent, false_positive=false_positive)
   236→    if not _validate_skip_requirements(
   237→        kind=kind,
   238→        attestation=attestation,
   239→        note=note,
   240→    ):
   241→        return
   242→
   243→    state_file = runtime.state_path
   244→    plan_file = _plan_file_for_state(state_file)
   245→    plan = load_plan(plan_file)
   246→    issue_ids = resolve_ids_from_patterns(state, patterns, plan=plan)
   247→    if not issue_ids:
   248→        print(colorize("  No matching issues found.", "yellow"))
   249→        return
   250→
   251→    # Bulk skip guard — prevent agents from draining the queue in one shot
   252→    if len(issue_ids) > _BULK_SKIP_THRESHOLD:
   253→        print(colorize(
   254→            f"  Bulk skip: {len(issue_ids)} items will be removed from the active queue.",
   255→            "yellow",
   256→        ), file=sys.stderr)
   257→        if not getattr(args, "confirm", False):
   258→            raise CommandError(
   259→                f"Skipping {len(issue_ids)} items requires --confirm. "
   260→                "Review the items first, or skip individually."
   261→            )
   262→
   263→    # For permanent/false_positive: delegate to state layer for score impact
   264→    state_data = _apply_state_skip_resolution(
   265→        kind=kind,
   266→        state_file=state_file,
   267→        issue_ids=issue_ids,
   268→        note=note,
   269→        attestation=attestation,
   270→    )
   271→
   272→    scan_count = state.get("scan_count", 0)
   273→    count = skip_items(
   274→        plan,
   275→        issue_ids,
   276→        kind=kind,
   277→        reason=reason,
   278→        note=note,
   279→        attestation=attestation,
   280→        review_after=review_after,
   281→        scan_count=scan_count,
   282→    )
   283→
   284→    # Log the skip action
   285→    append_log_entry(
   286→        plan,
   287→        "skip",
   288→        issue_ids=issue_ids,
   289→        actor="user",
   290→        note=note,
   291→        detail={"kind": kind, "reason": reason},
   292→    )
   293→    if state_data is not None:
   294→        _save_plan_state_transactional(
   295→            plan=plan,
   296→            plan_path=plan_file,
   297→            state_data=state_data,
   298→            state_path_value=state_file,
   299→        )
   300→    else:
   301→        save_plan(plan, plan_file)
   302→
   303→    print(colorize(f"  {SKIP_KIND_LABELS[kind]} {count} item(s).", "green"))
   304→    if review_after:
   305→        print(colorize(f"  Will re-surface after {review_after} scan(s).", "dim"))
   306→    print_user_message(
   307→        "Hey — if skipping was the right call, just continue with"
   308→        " what you were doing. If you think a broader re-triage is"
   309→        " needed, use `desloppify plan triage`. Run `desloppify"
   310→        " plan --help` to see all available plan tools. Otherwise"
   311→        " no need to reply, just keep going."
   312→    )
   313→
   314→
   315→def cmd_plan_unskip(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   316→    """Unskip issues — bring back to queue."""
   317→    runtime = command_runtime(args)
   318→    state = runtime.state
   319→    if not require_completed_scan(state):
   320→        return
   321→
   322→    patterns: list[str] = getattr(args, "patterns", [])
   323→
   324→    state_file = runtime.state_path
   325→    plan_file = _plan_file_for_state(state_file)
   326→    plan = load_plan(plan_file)
   327→    # For unskip we need to match against all statuses (skipped items may be wontfix/fp)
   328→    issue_ids = resolve_ids_from_patterns(state, patterns, plan=plan, status_filter="all")
   329→    if not issue_ids:
   330→        print(colorize("  No matching issues found.", "yellow"))
   331→        return
   332→
   333→    include_protected = bool(getattr(args, "force", False))
   334→    count, need_reopen, protected_kept = unskip_items(
   335→        plan, issue_ids, include_protected=include_protected,
   336→    )
   337→    unskipped_ids = [fid for fid in issue_ids if fid not in protected_kept]
   338→    append_log_entry(
   339→        plan, "unskip", issue_ids=unskipped_ids, actor="user",
   340→        detail={"need_reopen": need_reopen},
   341→    )
   342→
   343→    # Reopen permanent/false_positive items in state
   344→    reopened: list[str] = []
   345→    if need_reopen:
   346→        state_data = state_mod.load_state(state_file)
   347→        for fid in need_reopen:
   348→            reopened.extend(state_mod.resolve_issues(state_data, fid, "open"))
   349→        _save_plan_state_transactional(
   350→            plan=plan,
   351→            plan_path=plan_file,
   352→            state_data=state_data,
   353→            state_path_value=state_file,
   354→        )
   355→        print(colorize(f"  Reopened {len(reopened)} issue(s) in state.", "dim"))
   356→    else:
   357→        save_plan(plan, plan_file)
   358→
   359→    print(colorize(f"  Unskipped {count} item(s) — back in queue.", "green"))
   360→    if protected_kept:
   361→        print(colorize(
   362→            f"  Kept {len(protected_kept)} protected skip(s) "
   363→            f"(permanent/false_positive with notes). Use --force to override.",
   364→            "yellow",
   365→        ))
   366→
   367→
   368→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   369→# Reopen
   370→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   371→
   372→def cmd_plan_reopen(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   373→    """Reopen resolved issues from plan context."""
   374→    patterns: list[str] = getattr(args, "patterns", [])
   375→
   376→    raw_state_path = state_path(args)
   377→    state_file = raw_state_path if isinstance(raw_state_path, Path) else Path(raw_state_path) if raw_state_path else None
   378→    state_data = state_mod.load_state(state_file)
   379→    plan_file = _plan_file_for_state(state_file)
   380→
   381→    reopened: list[str] = []
   382→    for pattern in patterns:
   383→        reopened.extend(
   384→            state_mod.resolve_issues(state_data, pattern, "open")
   385→        )
   386→
   387→    if not reopened:
   388→        print(colorize("  No resolved issues matching: " + " ".join(patterns), "yellow"))
   389→        return
   390→
   391→    # Remove from skipped if present, and ensure all reopened IDs are in queue
   392→    plan = load_plan(plan_file)
   393→
   394→    # Remove from commit tracking uncommitted list
   395→    purge_uncommitted_ids(plan, reopened)
   396→
   397→    skipped = plan.get("skipped", {})
   398→    count = 0
   399→    order = set(plan.get("queue_order", []))
   400→    for fid in reopened:
   401→        if fid in skipped:
   402→            skipped.pop(fid)
   403→            count += 1
   404→        if fid not in order:
   405→            plan["queue_order"].append(fid)
   406→            order.add(fid)
   407→            count += 1
   408→    append_log_entry(
   409→        plan, "reopen", issue_ids=reopened, actor="user",
   410→    )
   411→    _save_plan_state_transactional(
   412→        plan=plan,
   413→        plan_path=plan_file,
   414→        state_data=state_data,
   415→        state_path_value=state_file,
   416→    )
   417→
   418→    print(colorize(f"  Reopened {len(reopened)} issue(s).", "green"))
   419→    if count:
   420→        print(colorize("  Plan updated: items moved back to queue.", "dim"))
   421→
   422→
   423→_CLUSTER_INDIVIDUAL_THRESHOLD = 10
   424→
   425→
   426→def _check_cluster_guard(patterns: list[str], plan: dict, state: dict) -> bool:
   427→    """Return True if blocked by cluster guard, False if OK to proceed."""
   428→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   429→    issues = state.get("issues", {})
   430→    for pattern in patterns:
   431→        if pattern in clusters:
   432→            cluster = clusters[pattern]
   433→            # Filter to alive issues only — stale IDs should not count
   434→            ids = [
   435→                fid for fid in cluster.get("issue_ids", [])
   436→                if fid in issues and issues[fid].get("status") == "open"
   437→            ]
   438→            if len(ids) == 0:
   439→                print(colorize(
   440→                    f"\n  Cluster '{pattern}' is empty — add items before marking it done.\n",
   441→                    "yellow",
   442→                ))
   443→                print(colorize(
   444→                    f"  Use: desloppify plan cluster add {pattern} <issue-id>",
   445→                    "dim",
   446→                ))
   447→                return True  # blocked
   448→            if len(ids) <= _CLUSTER_INDIVIDUAL_THRESHOLD:
   449→                _print_cluster_guard(pattern, ids, state)
   450→                return True  # blocked
   451→    return False  # OK
   452→
   453→
   454→def _print_cluster_guard(cluster_name: str, issue_ids: list[str], state: dict) -> None:
   455→    issues = state.get("issues", {})
   456→    print(colorize(
   457→        f"\n  Cluster '{cluster_name}' has {len(issue_ids)} item(s) — mark them done individually first:\n",
   458→        "yellow",
   459→    ))
   460→    for fid in issue_ids:
   461→        f = issues.get(fid, {})
   462→        summary = f.get("summary", "(no summary)")[:80]
   463→        detector = f.get("detector", "?")
   464→        print(f"    {fid}  [{detector}]  {summary}")
   465→    print(colorize(
   466→        "\n  Use: desloppify resolve <id> --status fixed --note '...' --attest '...'",
   467→        "dim",
   468→    ))
   469→    print(colorize(
   470→        "  Or mark each resolved: desloppify plan resolve <id> --note '...' --confirm\n",
   471→        "dim",
   472→    ))
   473→
   474→
   475→def _is_synthetic_id(fid: str) -> bool:
   476→    """Return True if the ID is a synthetic workflow/triage item, not a real issue."""
   477→    return fid.startswith("triage::") or fid.startswith("workflow::") or fid.startswith("subjective::")
   478→
   479→
   480→def _resolve_synthetic_ids(patterns: list[str]) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]:
   481→    """Separate synthetic IDs from real issue patterns.
   482→
   483→    Returns (synthetic_ids, remaining_patterns).
   484→    """
   485→    synthetic = [p for p in patterns if _is_synthetic_id(p)]
   486→    remaining = [p for p in patterns if not _is_synthetic_id(p)]
   487→    return synthetic, remaining
   488→
   489→
   490→def _blocked_triage_stages(plan: dict) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
   491→    """Return ``{stage_id: [blocked_by_ids]}`` for triage stages that can't run yet.
   492→
   493→    Uses the dependency graph and confirmed-stage metadata directly —
   494→    no state needed, no queue item construction.
   495→    """
   496→    order_set = set(plan.get("queue_order", []))
   497→    present = order_set & TRIAGE_IDS
   498→    if not present:
   499→        return {}
   500→
   501→    confirmed = set(plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {}).get("triage_stages", {}).keys())
   502→    stage_names = ("observe", "reflect", "organize", "commit")
   503→
   504→    blocked: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
   505→    for sid, name in zip(TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS, stage_names, strict=False):
   506→        if sid not in present or name in confirmed:
   507→            continue
   508→        deps = TRIAGE_STAGE_DEPENDENCIES.get(name, set())
   509→        unmet = sorted(
   510→            f"triage::{dep}" for dep in deps
   511→            if f"triage::{dep}" in present and dep not in confirmed
   512→        )
   513→        if unmet:
   514→            blocked[sid] = unmet
   515→    return blocked
   516→
   517→
   518→def cmd_plan_resolve(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   519→    """Mark issues as fixed — delegates to cmd_resolve for rich UX."""
   520→    patterns: list[str] = getattr(args, "patterns", [])
   521→    attestation: str | None = getattr(args, "attest", None)
   522→    note: str | None = getattr(args, "note", None)
   523→
   524→    # --confirm: auto-generate attestation from --note
   525→    if getattr(args, "confirm", False):
   526→        if not note:
   527→            print(colorize("  --confirm requires --note to describe what you did.", "red"))
   528→            return
   529→        attestation = f"I have actually {note} and I am not gaming the score."
   530→        args.attest = attestation
   531→
   532→    # Handle synthetic IDs (triage::*, workflow::*, subjective::*) directly
   533→    synthetic_ids, real_patterns = _resolve_synthetic_ids(patterns)
   534→    if synthetic_ids:
   535→        plan = load_plan()
   536→        # Validate triage dependency chain
   537→        blocked_map = _blocked_triage_stages(plan)
   538→        for sid in synthetic_ids:
   539→            if sid in blocked_map:
   540→                deps = ", ".join(b.replace("triage::", "") for b in blocked_map[sid])
   541→                print(colorize(f"  Cannot resolve {sid} — blocked by: {deps}", "red"))
   542→                print(colorize("  Complete those stages first, or use --force-resolve to override.", "dim"))
   543→                if not getattr(args, "force_resolve", False):
   544→                    return
   545→
   546→        # Gate workflow items behind triage completion
   547→        GATED_WORKFLOW_IDS = {WORKFLOW_SCORE_CHECKPOINT_ID, WORKFLOW_CREATE_PLAN_ID}
   548→        gated_ids = [sid for sid in synthetic_ids if sid in GATED_WORKFLOW_IDS]
   549→        if gated_ids:
   550→            force = getattr(args, "force_resolve", False)
   551→            meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   552→            # Triage is complete if last_completed_at is set (stages archive on --complete)
   553→            triage_ever_completed = bool(meta.get("last_completed_at"))
   554→            if triage_ever_completed:
   555→                # --complete archives stages and sets last_completed_at → all 4 done
   556→                missing: set[str] = set()
   557→            else:
   558→                confirmed_stages = set(meta.get("triage_stages", {}).keys())
   559→                required_stages = {"observe", "reflect", "organize", "commit"}
   560→                missing = required_stages - confirmed_stages
   561→
   562→            if missing and not force:
   563→                # Auto-inject triage stages if not already in queue
   564→                if not has_triage_in_queue(plan):
   565→                    inject_triage_stages(plan)
   566→                    meta.setdefault("triage_stages", {})
   567→                    plan["epic_triage_meta"] = meta
   568→                    save_plan(plan)
   569→
   570→                # Print targeted error based on which stage is next
   571→                stage_order = ["observe", "reflect", "organize", "commit"]
   572→                next_stage = next((s for s in stage_order if s in missing), "observe")
   573→
   574→                for wid in gated_ids:
   575→                    print(colorize(f"  Cannot resolve {wid} — triage not complete.", "red"))
   576→                print()
   577→
   578→                if next_stage == "observe":
   579→                    print(colorize("  You must analyze the findings before resolving this.", "yellow"))
   580→                    print(colorize("  Start by examining themes, root causes, and contradictions:", "dim"))
   581→                    print(colorize('    desloppify plan triage --stage observe --report "..."', "dim"))
   582→                    print()
   583→                    print(colorize("  The report must be 100+ chars describing what you found.", "dim"))
   584→                elif next_stage == "reflect":
   585→                    print(colorize("  Observe is done. Now compare against previously completed work:", "yellow"))
   586→                    print(colorize('    desloppify plan triage --stage reflect --report "..."', "dim"))
   587→                    print()
   588→                    print(colorize("  The report must mention recurring dimensions if any exist.", "dim"))
   589→                elif next_stage == "organize":
   590→                    print(colorize("  Reflect is done. Now create clusters and prioritize:", "yellow"))
   591→                    print(colorize('    desloppify plan cluster create <name> --description "..."', "dim"))
   592→                    print(colorize("    desloppify plan cluster add <name> <issue-patterns>", "dim"))
   593→                    print(colorize('    desloppify plan cluster update <name> --steps "step1" "step2"', "dim"))
   594→                    print(colorize('    desloppify plan triage --stage organize --report "..."', "dim"))
   595→                    print()
   596→                    print(colorize("  All manual clusters must have descriptions and action_steps.", "dim"))
   597→                elif next_stage == "commit":
   598→                    print(colorize("  Organize is done. Finalize the execution plan:", "yellow"))
   599→                    print(colorize('    desloppify plan triage --complete --strategy "..."', "dim"))
   600→
   601→                print()
   602→                print(colorize(f"  Remaining stages: {', '.join(sorted(missing))}", "dim"))
   603→                print(colorize(
   604→                    "  To skip triage: --force-resolve --note 'reason for skipping triage'",
   605→                    "dim",
   606→                ))
   607→
   608→                # Log the blocked attempt
   609→                append_log_entry(
   610→                    plan, "workflow_blocked",
   611→                    issue_ids=gated_ids, actor="user",
   612→                    note=note,
   613→                    detail={"missing_stages": sorted(missing), "next_stage": next_stage},
   614→                )
   615→                save_plan(plan)
   616→                return
   617→
   618→            if missing and force:
   619→                # Force-resolve: require substantial note, log prominently
   620→                if not note or len(note.strip()) < 50:
   621→                    print(colorize(
   622→                        f"  --force-resolve still requires --note (min 50 chars) explaining "
   623→                        f"why you're skipping triage.",
   624→                        "red",
   625→                    ))
   626→                    return
   627→                print(colorize(
   628→                    "  WARNING: Skipping triage requirement — this is logged.",
   629→                    "yellow",
   630→                ))
   631→                append_log_entry(
   632→                    plan, "workflow_force_skip",
   633→                    issue_ids=gated_ids, actor="user",
   634→                    note=note,
   635→                    detail={"forced": True, "missing_stages": sorted(missing)},
   636→                )
   637→                save_plan(plan)
   638→                # Fall through to scan gate / purge_ids below
   639→
   640→        # Gate workflow items behind scan completion
   641→        if gated_ids:
   642→            scan_count_at_start = plan.get("scan_count_at_plan_start")
   643→            if scan_count_at_start is not None:
   644→                resolved_state_path = state_path(args)
   645→                state_data = state_mod.load_state(resolved_state_path)
   646→                current_scan_count = int(state_data.get("scan_count", 0) or 0)
   647→                scan_ran = current_scan_count > scan_count_at_start
   648→                scan_skipped = plan.get("scan_gate_skipped", False)
   649→
   650→                if not scan_ran and not scan_skipped and not force:
   651→                    for wid in gated_ids:
   652→                        print(colorize(
   653→                            f"  Cannot resolve {wid} — no scan has run this cycle.",
   654→                            "red",
   655→                        ))
   656→                    print()
   657→                    print(colorize(
   658→                        "  You must run a scan before resolving workflow items:",

   801→def cmd_plan_scan_gate(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   802→    """Check or skip the scan requirement for workflow items."""
   803→    skip = getattr(args, "skip", False)
   804→    note: str | None = getattr(args, "note", None)
   805→
   806→    plan = load_plan()
   807→    scan_count_at_start = plan.get("scan_count_at_plan_start")
   808→
   809→    if scan_count_at_start is None:
   810→        print(colorize("  No active plan cycle (plan_start_scores not seeded).", "dim"))
   811→        print(colorize("  Scan gate is not applicable — workflow items gate themselves.", "dim"))
   812→        return
   813→
   814→    resolved_state_path = state_path(args)
   815→    state_data = state_mod.load_state(resolved_state_path)
   816→    current_scan_count = int(state_data.get("scan_count", 0) or 0)
   817→    scan_ran = current_scan_count > scan_count_at_start
   818→    scan_skipped = plan.get("scan_gate_skipped", False)
   819→
   820→    if not skip:
   821→        # Status check
   822→        if scan_ran:
   823→            print(colorize("  Scan gate: PASSED", "green"))
   824→            print(colorize(
   825→                f"  Scans at cycle start: {scan_count_at_start}  "
   826→                f"Current: {current_scan_count}",
   827→                "dim",
   828→            ))
   829→        elif scan_skipped:
   830→            print(colorize("  Scan gate: SKIPPED (manually)", "yellow"))
   831→        else:
   832→            print(colorize("  Scan gate: BLOCKED", "red"))
   833→            print(colorize(
   834→                f"  Scans at cycle start: {scan_count_at_start}  "
   835→                f"Current: {current_scan_count}",
   836→                "dim",
   837→            ))
   838→            print(colorize("  Run: desloppify scan", "dim"))
   839→            print(colorize(
   840→                '  Or:  desloppify plan scan-gate --skip --note "reason"',
   841→                "dim",
   842→            ))
   843→        return
   844→
   845→    # --skip mode
   846→    if scan_ran:
   847→        print(colorize("  Scan already ran this cycle — no skip needed.", "green"))
   848→        return
   849→
   850→    if not note or len(note.strip()) < 50:
   851→        print(colorize(
   852→            "  --skip requires --note with at least 50 chars explaining why.",
   853→            "red",
   854→        ))
   855→        return
   856→
   857→    plan["scan_gate_skipped"] = True
   858→    append_log_entry(
   859→        plan, "scan_gate_skip",
   860→        actor="user",
   861→        note=note,
   862→        detail={
   863→            "scan_count_at_start": scan_count_at_start,
   864→            "current_scan_count": current_scan_count,
   865→        },
   866→    )
   867→    save_plan(plan)
   868→    print(colorize("  Scan requirement marked as satisfied (logged).", "yellow"))
   869→

   195→def _print_score_section(state, scores, plan, target_strict_score, ctx=None):
   196→    """Print score header: frozen plan-start or live score with queue breakdown."""
   197→    plan_start_strict = get_plan_start_strict(plan)
   198→
   199→    # Build breakdown — needed for both display mode decision and rendering.

   201→    try:
   202→        breakdown = plan_aware_queue_breakdown(state, plan, context=ctx)
   203→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS as exc:
   204→        _logger.debug("Plan-aware queue count failed: %s", exc)
   205→
   206→    mode = score_display_mode(breakdown, plan_start_strict)
   207→
   208→    if mode is ScoreDisplayMode.FROZEN:
   209→        print_frozen_score_with_queue_context(
   210→            breakdown,
   211→            frozen_strict=plan_start_strict,
   212→            live_score=scores.strict,
   213→        )
   214→    else:
   215→        # LIVE or PHASE_TRANSITION: show current live scores
   216→        for line, style in score_summary_lines(
   217→            overall_score=scores.overall,
   218→            objective_score=scores.objective,
   219→            strict_score=scores.strict,
   220→            verified_strict_score=scores.verified,
   221→            target_strict=target_strict_score,
   222→        ):
   223→            print(colorize(line, style))
   224→        if breakdown is not None and breakdown.queue_total > 0:
   225→            block = format_queue_block(breakdown)
   226→            for text, style in block:
   227→                print(colorize(text, style))
   228→        if mode is ScoreDisplayMode.PHASE_TRANSITION:
   229→            print_objective_drained_banner(plan_start_strict, breakdown.queue_total, breakdown)
   230→
   231→    return breakdown

    55→            chronic=bool(getattr(args, "chronic", False)),
    56→            no_budget=bool(getattr(args, "no_budget", False)),
    57→            output_file=getattr(args, "output", None),
    58→            top=int(getattr(args, "top", 20) or 20),
    59→        )
    60→
    61→
    62→def _handle_special_entity_views(
    63→    *,
    64→    entity,
    65→    state: dict,
    66→    config: dict,
    67→    lang_name: str | None,
    68→    pattern_raw: str,
    69→) -> bool:
    70→    if entity.kind == "special_view" and entity.pattern.strip().lower() == "concerns":
    71→        _show_concerns(state, lang_name)
    72→        return True
    73→    if entity.kind == "dimension" and entity.is_subjective:
    74→        _render_subjective_dimension(state, config, entity, pattern_raw)
    75→        return True
    76→    return False
    77→
    78→
    79→def _load_entity_matches(
    80→    *,
    81→    state: dict,
    82→    entity,
    83→    pattern: str,
    84→    status_filter: str,
    85→    scope: str | None,
    86→    chronic: bool,
    87→) -> tuple[str, list[dict]] | None:
    88→    if entity.kind != "dimension" or entity.is_subjective:
    89→        return pattern, load_matches(
    90→            state, scope=scope, status_filter=status_filter, chronic=chronic
    91→        )
    92→    matches = _load_dimension_issues(state, entity, status_filter)
    93→    if not matches:
    94→        _render_clean_mechanical_dimension(state, entity)
    95→        return None
    96→    return entity.display_name, matches
    97→
    98→
    99→def _active_plan_or_none() -> dict | None:
   100→    try:
   101→        plan = load_plan()
   102→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS:
   103→        return None
   104→    if plan.get("queue_order") or plan.get("clusters"):
   105→        return plan
   106→    return None
   107→
   108→
   109→def cmd_show(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   110→    """Show all issues for a file, directory, detector, or pattern."""
   111→    runtime = command_runtime(args)
   112→    state = runtime.state
   113→    config = runtime.config
   114→
   115→    if not require_completed_scan(state):
   116→        return
   117→
   118→    skill_warning = check_skill_version()
   119→    if skill_warning:
   120→        print(colorize(f"  {skill_warning}", "yellow"))
   121→    config_warning = check_config_staleness(config)
   122→    if config_warning:
   123→        print(colorize(f"  {config_warning}", "yellow"))
   124→
   125→    print_triage_guardrail_info(state=state)
   126→
   127→    opts = ShowOptions.from_args(args)
   128→
   129→    ok, pattern, status_filter, scope = resolve_show_scope(args)
   130→    if not ok or pattern is None:
   131→        return
   132→
   133→    lang = resolve_lang(args)
   134→    lang_name = lang.name if lang else None
   135→    narrative = compute_narrative(
   136→        state,
   137→        context=NarrativeContext(lang=lang_name, command="show"),
   138→    )
   139→
   140→    entity = resolve_entity(pattern, state)
   141→    if _handle_special_entity_views(
   142→        entity=entity,
   143→        state=state,
   144→        config=config,
   145→        lang_name=lang_name,
   146→        pattern_raw=opts.pattern_raw,
   147→    ):
   148→        return
   149→
   150→    match_result = _load_entity_matches(
   151→        state=state,
   152→        entity=entity,
   153→        pattern=pattern,
   154→        status_filter=status_filter,
   155→        scope=scope,
   156→        chronic=opts.chronic,
   157→    )
   158→    if match_result is None:
   159→        return
   160→    pattern, matches = match_result
   161→
   162→    if not matches:
   163→        _render_no_matches(entity, pattern, status_filter, narrative, state, config)
   164→        return
   165→
   166→    (
   167→        surfaced_matches,
   168→        hidden_by_detector,
   169→        noise_budget,
   170→        global_noise_budget,
   171→        budget_warning,
   172→    ) = resolve_noise(
   173→        config,
   174→        matches,
   175→        no_budget=opts.no_budget,
   176→    )
   177→    hidden_total = sum(hidden_by_detector.values())
   178→
   179→    payload = build_show_payload(
   180→        surfaced_matches,
   181→        pattern,
   182→        status_filter,
   183→        ShowPayloadMeta(
   184→            total_matches=len(matches),
   185→            hidden_by_detector=hidden_by_detector,
   186→            noise_budget=noise_budget,
   187→            global_noise_budget=global_noise_budget,
   188→        ),
   189→    )
   190→    write_query({"command": "show", **payload, "narrative": narrative})
   191→
   192→    if opts.output_file:
   193→        if write_show_output_file(opts.output_file, payload, len(surfaced_matches)):
   194→            return
   195→        raise CommandError("Failed to write output file")
   196→
   197→    render_issues(
   198→        surfaced_matches,
   199→        pattern=pattern,
   200→        status_filter=status_filter,
   201→        show_code=opts.show_code,
   202→        top=opts.top,
   203→        hidden_by_detector=hidden_by_detector,
   204→        hidden_total=hidden_total,
   205→        noise_budget=noise_budget,
   206→        global_noise_budget=global_noise_budget,
   207→        budget_warning=budget_warning,
   208→    )
   209→    plan_active = _active_plan_or_none()
   210→    show_agent_plan(narrative, surfaced_matches, plan=plan_active)
   211→    show_subjective_followup(
   212→        state,
   213→        target_strict_score_from_config(config),
   214→    )
   215→
   216→    _render_subjective_views_guide(entity)
   217→
   218→
   219→__all__ = ["cmd_show"]
   220→

    14→def _serialize_cluster_member(member: Mapping[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:

    28→def serialize_item(item: Mapping[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    29→    """Build a serializable output dict from a queue item."""
    30→    # Cluster meta-items get their own serialization
    31→    if item.get("kind") == "cluster":
    32→        members_raw = item.get("members", [])
    33→        serialized_members = [

    47→            "detector": item.get("detector"),

    49→        if member_count > len(serialized_members):

    52→        serialized_cluster["primary_command"] = item.get("primary_command")

    55→        action_steps = item.get("action_steps") or []
    56→        if action_steps:

   100→def build_query_payload(
   101→    queue: Mapping[str, Any],
   102→    items: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]],
   103→    *,
   104→    command: str,
   105→    narrative: Mapping[str, Any] | None,
   106→    plan: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
   107→) -> dict[str, Any]:
   108→    """Build JSON payload for query.json and non-terminal output modes."""
   109→    serialized = [serialize_item(item) for item in items]
   110→    queue_section: dict[str, Any] = {
   111→        "total": queue.get("total", len(items)),
   112→    }
   113→
   114→    payload: dict[str, Any] = {
   115→        "command": command,
   116→        "items": serialized,
   117→        "queue": queue_section,
   118→        "narrative": narrative,
   119→        "agent_notes": [
   120→            "Do NOT use `desloppify plan skip` unless the user explicitly asks you to skip an item.",
   121→            "If you cannot fix an item, report it and move to the next one.",
   122→            "For cluster items: if the autofix_hint finds 0 results, drill into individual issues with the primary_command.",
   123→        ],
   124→    }
   125→
   126→    if plan and (
   127→        plan.get("queue_order")
   128→        or plan.get("skipped")
   129→        or plan.get("clusters")
   130→    ):
   131→        clusters_summary = []
   132→        for name, cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items():
   133→            member_ids = set(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   134→            clusters_summary.append({
   135→                "name": name,
   136→                "description": cluster.get("description"),
   137→                "item_count": len(member_ids),
   138→            })
   139→        payload["plan"] = {
   140→            "active": True,
   141→            "focus": plan.get("active_cluster"),
   142→            "clusters": clusters_summary,
   143→            "total_ordered": len(plan.get("queue_order", [])),
   144→            "total_skipped": len(plan.get("skipped", {})),
   145→            "plan_overrides_narrative": True,
   146→        }
   147→
   148→    return payload
   149→
   150→
   151→def render_markdown(items: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]) -> str:
   152→    """Render queue items as markdown."""
   153→    lines = [
   154→        "# Desloppify Next Queue",
   155→        "",
   156→        "| Kind | Confidence | Summary | Command |",
   157→        "|------|------------|---------|---------|",
   158→    ]
   159→    for item in items:
   160→        kind = item.get("kind", "issue")
   161→        conf = item.get("confidence", "medium")
   162→        summary = item.get("summary", "").replace("|", "\\|")
   163→        command = (item.get("primary_command", "") or "").replace("|", "\\|")
   164→        lines.append(f"| {kind} | {conf} | {summary} | {command} |")
   165→    lines.append("")
   166→    return "\n".join(lines)
   167→
   168→
   169→def write_output_file(
   170→    output_file: str,
   171→    payload: dict[str, Any],
   172→    item_count: int,
   173→    *,
   174→    safe_write_text_fn,
   175→    colorize_fn,
   176→) -> bool:
   177→    """Persist payload to file and print success/failure hints."""
   178→    try:
   179→        safe_write_text_fn(output_file, json.dumps(payload, indent=2) + "\n")
   180→        print(colorize_fn(f"Wrote {item_count} items to {output_file}", "green"))
   181→    except OSError as exc:
   182→        payload["output_error"] = str(exc)
   183→        print_write_error(output_file, exc, label="next output")
   184→        return False
   185→    return True
   186→
   187→
   188→def emit_non_terminal_output(
   189→    output_format: str,
   190→    payload: dict[str, Any],
   191→    items: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]],
   192→) -> bool:
   193→    """Render JSON/markdown output variants."""
   194→    renderers = {
   195→        "json": lambda: print(json.dumps(payload, indent=2)),
   196→        "md": lambda: print(render_markdown(items)),
   197→    }
   198→    renderer = renderers.get(output_format)
   199→    if renderer is None:
   200→        return False
   201→    renderer()
   202→    return True
   203→
   204→

   207→    "emit_non_terminal_output",
   208→    "render_markdown",

   210→    "write_output_file",

1→"""Metadata and logging mutations for plan operations."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from desloppify.engine._plan.schema import (
     6→    ExecutionLogEntry,
     7→    PlanModel,
     8→    ensure_plan_defaults,
     9→)
    10→from desloppify.engine._state.schema import utc_now
    11→
    12→_DEFAULT_MAX_LOG_ENTRIES = 10000
    13→
    14→
    15→def _get_log_cap() -> int:
    16→    """Read execution_log_max_entries from config. Returns 0 for unlimited."""
    17→    try:
    18→        from desloppify.base.config import load_config
    19→
    20→        config = load_config()
    21→        value = config.get("execution_log_max_entries", _DEFAULT_MAX_LOG_ENTRIES)
    22→        return max(0, int(value))
    23→    except (ImportError, OSError, ValueError, TypeError):
    24→        return _DEFAULT_MAX_LOG_ENTRIES
    25→
    26→
    27→def append_log_entry(
    28→    plan: PlanModel,
    29→    action: str,
    30→    *,
    31→    issue_ids: list[str] | None = None,
    32→    cluster_name: str | None = None,
    33→    actor: str = "user",
    34→    note: str | None = None,
    35→    detail: dict | None = None,
    36→) -> None:
    37→    """Append a structured entry to the plan's execution log."""
    38→    log = plan.get("execution_log", [])
    39→    entry: ExecutionLogEntry = {
    40→        "timestamp": utc_now(),
    41→        "action": action,
    42→        "issue_ids": issue_ids or [],
    43→        "cluster_name": cluster_name,
    44→        "actor": actor,
    45→        "note": note,
    46→        "detail": detail or {},
    47→    }
    48→    log.append(entry)
    49→    cap = _get_log_cap()
    50→    if cap > 0 and len(log) > cap:
    51→        plan["execution_log"] = log[-cap:]
    52→
    53→
    54→def describe_issue(
    55→    plan: PlanModel, issue_id: str, description: str | None
    56→) -> None:
    57→    """Set or clear an augmented description on a issue."""
    58→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
    59→    now = utc_now()
    60→    overrides = plan["overrides"]
    61→    if issue_id not in overrides:
    62→        overrides[issue_id] = {"issue_id": issue_id, "created_at": now}
    63→    overrides[issue_id]["description"] = description
    64→    overrides[issue_id]["updated_at"] = now
    65→
    66→
    67→def annotate_issue(
    68→    plan: PlanModel, issue_id: str, note: str | None
    69→) -> None:
    70→    """Set or clear a note on a issue."""
    71→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
    72→    now = utc_now()
    73→    overrides = plan["overrides"]
    74→    if issue_id not in overrides:
    75→        overrides[issue_id] = {"issue_id": issue_id, "created_at": now}
    76→    overrides[issue_id]["note"] = note
    77→    overrides[issue_id]["updated_at"] = now
    78→
    79→
    80→__all__ = ["annotate_issue", "append_log_entry", "describe_issue"]

    62→def _capture_cluster_context(
    63→    plan: dict, resolved_ids: list[str],
    64→) -> ClusterContext:
    65→    """Determine cluster membership for resolved issues, pre-purge."""
    66→    clusters = plan.get("clusters") or {}
    67→    overrides = plan.get("overrides") or {}
    68→    # Find the cluster the first resolved issue belongs to
    69→    cluster_name: str | None = None
    70→    for rid in resolved_ids:
    71→        ov = overrides.get(rid)
    72→        if ov and ov.get("cluster"):
    73→            cluster_name = ov["cluster"]
    74→            break
    75→    if not cluster_name or cluster_name not in clusters:
    76→        return ClusterContext(cluster_name=None, cluster_completed=False, cluster_remaining=0)
    77→    # Count how many will remain after these ids are removed
    78→    current_ids = set(clusters[cluster_name].get("issue_ids") or [])
    79→    remaining = current_ids - set(resolved_ids)
    80→    return ClusterContext(
    81→        cluster_name=cluster_name,
    82→        cluster_completed=len(remaining) == 0,
    83→        cluster_remaining=len(remaining),
    84→    )

## Analysis

Here are the answers to your three questions:

### 1. Is `opts.output_format` available in `cmd_next()` before calling `_build_and_render_queue`?

**No, not directly in `cmd_next()`.** The flow is:
- Line 124 in `cmd_next()`: `print_triage_guardrail_info(state=state)` is called **unconditionally**
- Line 125: `_build_and_render_queue(args, state, config)` is called
- Inside `_build_and_render_queue()`, line 211: `opts = NextOptions.from_args(args)` extracts the format
- Line 280: `_emit_requested_output(opts, payload, items)` checks the format

**The guardrail warning prints BEFORE the format check happens.** It always prints to stdout regardless of `--format json`.

### 2. Could we pass format info to `print_triage_guardrail_info` to suppress for JSON, or should we restructure the call order?

Both approaches are viable:

**Option A: Pass format to `print_triage_guardrail_info`** (minimal change)
- Add an optional `output_format: str = "terminal"` parameter to `print_triage_guardrail_info()`
- Skip printing if `output_format != "terminal"`
- Call it as: `print_triage_guardrail_info(state=state, output_format=opts.output_format)` after extracting `opts`
- Extract `NextOptions.from_args(args)` at the top of `cmd_next()`, before `print_triage_guardrail_info`

**Option B: Restructure call order** (cleaner separation)
- Move `print_triage_guardrail_info()` call **inside** `_build_and_render_queue()`, after `opts = NextOptions.from_args(args)` on line 211
- Pass `output_format` parameter to the function
- This keeps format-aware logic centralized in `_build_and_render_queue()`

### 3. Are there other commands that call `print_triage_guardrail_info` before a potential JSON output path?

**Yes, two commands have the same pattern:**

1. **`status/cmd.py`** (lines 73–112):
   - Lines 73–87: Early `if getattr(args, "json", False):` check that returns early with JSON output
   - **BUT** line 112 calls `print_triage_guardrail_info()` AFTER that early return
   - So `status --json` does NOT have this bug (the early return prevents the guardrail print)

2. **`show/cmd.py`** (lines 109–125):
   - Line 125: `print_triage_guardrail_info(state=state)` is called unconditionally
   - Lines 192–195: Later, there's an `output_file` check that can return early
   - **BUT there is no format option for `show` command** — it only has `--output` (file) not `--format`
   - So `show` doesn't have the JSON format bug, but it's still printing guardrails unconditionally

**Summary:** The `next` command is the only one with this bug because:
- `status` guards with an early `--json` return before the guardrail print
- `show` doesn't have a `--format` flag at all
- `next` prints the guardrail unconditionally, then checks format later

The cleanest fix for `next` is **Option A** — extract `NextOptions` first, then pass format to `print_triage_guardrail_info()`.

1→"""Parse and format numbered-steps text files for ActionStep data."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import re
     6→from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
     7→
     8→if TYPE_CHECKING:
     9→    from desloppify.engine._plan.schema import ActionStep
    10→
    11→_STEP_HEADER_RE = re.compile(r"^(\d+)\.\s+(.+)$")
    12→_REFS_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*Refs?:\s*(.+)$", re.IGNORECASE)
    13→
    14→
    15→def parse_steps_file(text: str) -> list[ActionStep]:
    16→    """Parse a numbered-steps text format into ActionStep dicts.
    17→
    18→    Format::
    19→
    20→        1. Step title here
    21→           Detail lines indented by 2+ spaces.
    22→           More detail.
    23→           Refs: abc123, def456
    24→
    25→        2. Another step
    26→           Its detail block.
    27→    """
    28→    steps: list[ActionStep] = []
    29→    current: ActionStep | None = None
    30→    detail_lines: list[str] = []
    31→
    32→    def _flush() -> None:
    33→        nonlocal current, detail_lines
    34→        if current is None:
    35→            return
    36→        detail = "\n".join(detail_lines).strip()
    37→        if detail:
    38→            current["detail"] = detail
    39→        steps.append(current)
    40→        current = None
    41→        detail_lines = []
    42→
    43→    for line in text.splitlines():
    44→        m = _STEP_HEADER_RE.match(line)
    45→        if m:
    46→            _flush()
    47→            current = {"title": m.group(2).strip()}
    48→            continue
    49→
    50→        if current is None:
    51→            continue
    52→
    53→        # Indented continuation line
    54→        if line and (line[0] == " " or line[0] == "\t"):
    55→            stripped = line.strip()
    56→            ref_match = _REFS_RE.match(line)
    57→            if ref_match:
    58→                refs = [r.strip() for r in ref_match.group(1).split(",") if r.strip()]
    59→                current.setdefault("issue_refs", []).extend(refs)
    60→            else:
    61→                detail_lines.append(stripped)
    62→        elif line.strip() == "":
    63→            # Blank line within detail — preserve it
    64→            if detail_lines:
    65→                detail_lines.append("")
    66→        # Non-indented non-blank line that isn't a step header: ignore
    67→
    68→    _flush()
    69→    return steps
    70→
    71→
    72→def format_steps(steps: list[str | dict]) -> str:
    73→    """Format a list of ActionStep dicts (or legacy strings) into numbered-steps text.
    74→
    75→    Round-trips with ``parse_steps_file``: ``parse_steps_file(format_steps(steps))``
    76→    reproduces the same data (modulo whitespace normalization).
    77→    """
    78→    lines: list[str] = []
    79→    for i, step in enumerate(steps, 1):
    80→        if isinstance(step, str):
    81→            lines.append(f"{i}. {step}")
    82→        elif isinstance(step, dict):
    83→            title = step.get("title", "")
    84→            done = step.get("done", False)
    85→            prefix = "[x] " if done else ""
    86→            lines.append(f"{i}. {prefix}{title}")
    87→            detail = step.get("detail", "")
    88→            if detail:
    89→                for dline in detail.splitlines():
    90→                    lines.append(f"   {dline}")
    91→            refs = step.get("issue_refs", [])
    92→            if refs:
    93→                lines.append(f"   Refs: {', '.join(refs)}")
    94→        lines.append("")
    95→    return "\n".join(lines)
    96→
    97→
    98→def normalize_step(step: str | dict) -> dict:
    99→    """Ensure a step is an ActionStep dict. Wraps plain strings."""
   100→    if isinstance(step, dict):
   101→        return step
   102→    return {"title": step}
   103→
   104→
   105→def step_summary(step: str | dict) -> str:
   106→    """Return a one-line summary of a step for display."""
   107→    if isinstance(step, str):
   108→        return step
   109→    return step.get("title", "")
   110→
   111→
   112→__all__ = [
   113→    "format_steps",
   114→    "normalize_step",
   115→    "parse_steps_file",
   116→    "step_summary",
   117→]
   118→

## Summary: `desloppify plan resolve` Flow & Auto-Step-Completion Integration Points

Based on my thorough analysis of the codebase, here's the complete flow for the `desloppify plan resolve` command and where auto-step-completion logic can be hooked in:

### 1. **Resolve Command Handler**

**Location:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/override_handlers.py`, function `cmd_plan_resolve` (lines 518-761)

**Key Flow:**
- Accepts patterns (issue IDs, cluster names, or synthetic IDs like `triage::*`, `workflow::*`)
- Delegates to `cmd_resolve` (from `app/commands/resolve/cmd.py`) for real issues
- Handles synthetic IDs (triage/workflow items) directly by calling `purge_ids(plan, synthetic_ids)`
- Always calls `append_log_entry(plan, "done", issue_ids=..., actor="user", note=note)` to log the resolution

### 2. **Post-Resolution Plan Update**

**Location:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/resolve/cmd.py`, function `_update_living_plan_after_resolve` (lines 97-138)

**This is where REAL issues get resolved.** The function:
- Captures cluster context (which cluster, if any, the issue belongs to)
- Calls `purge_ids(plan, all_resolved)` to remove resolved issues from the queue
- Appends a `"resolve"` log entry with:
  - `issue_ids`: the resolved issue IDs
  - `actor`: "user"
  - `note`: the user's note
  - `detail`: `{"status": args.status, "attestation": attestation}`
- If the cluster is now empty, appends a `"cluster_done"` log entry
- Updates commit tracking (adds to uncommitted on "fixed", removes on "open")

### 3. **State and Plan Data Available at Resolution Point**

When `append_log_entry` is called:
- **Plan object** contains:
  - `clusters`: All clusters with their `action_steps` (list of `ActionStep` dicts)
  - `queue_order`: Active queue of issue IDs
  - `overrides`: Per-issue metadata including cluster assignment
  - `execution_log`: The current execution log
  
- **Resolved issue IDs**: Both as a list parameter and extractable from the resolved patterns

- **Cluster membership**: Available via `plan["overrides"][issue_id].get("cluster")`

### 4. **ActionStep Schema**

**Location:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/schema.py` (lines 42-46)

```python
class ActionStep(TypedDict, total=False):
    title: Required[str]        # Short summary, 1 line
    detail: str                 # Long description, paragraphs OK
    issue_refs: list[str]       # Issue ID suffixes this step addresses ← KEY!
    done: bool                  # Completion tracking (default False)
```

**Critical note:** `issue_refs` stores issue ID **suffixes** (e.g., "abc123", not "epic/foo" or "cluster_name"). This is how steps track which issues they address.

### 5. **Where Clusters and Steps Live**

**Location:** `plan["clusters"][cluster_name]["action_steps"]`

Structure:
```python
plan["clusters"]["my-cluster"]["action_steps"] = [
    {
        "title": "Fix logging",
        "detail": "Add debug output to verify...",
        "issue_refs": ["abc123", "def456"],
        "done": False
    },
    {
        "title": "Deploy to staging",
        "issue_refs": ["abc123"],
        "done": False
    }
]
```

### 6. **How Steps Are Currently Marked Done (Manually)**

**Location:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/cluster_handlers.py`, function `_cmd_cluster_update` (lines 674-685)

Users manually call:
```bash
desloppify plan cluster update <cluster-name> --done-step <step-number>
```

This sets `step["done"] = True` on the step dict.

---

### **INTEGRATION POINT: WHERE TO ADD AUTO-STEP-COMPLETION**

**Best location:** In `_update_living_plan_after_resolve` in `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/resolve/cmd.py`, **right after the `purge_ids()` call** (line 110).

**Algorithm:**

```python
def _auto_complete_steps(plan: dict, resolved_ids: list[str]) -> int:
    """Mark action steps as done when all their issue_refs are resolved.
    
    Returns count of steps marked done.
    """
    completed_count = 0
    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
    
    for cluster in clusters.values():
        steps = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
        # Get the set of issues still in queue
        queue_set = set(plan.get("queue_order", []))
        
        for step in steps:
            if isinstance(step, dict) and not step.get("done"):
                issue_refs = step.get("issue_refs", [])
                if issue_refs:
                    # Check if all refs are gone from the queue
                    if all(ref not in queue_set for ref in issue_refs):
                        step["done"] = True
                        completed_count += 1
    
    return completed_count
```

**Call it like:**
```python
# In _update_living_plan_after_resolve, after purge_ids():
purged = purge_ids(plan, all_resolved)
auto_completed = _auto_complete_steps(plan, all_resolved)  # NEW
if auto_completed > 0:
    append_log_entry(
        plan,
        "auto_complete_steps",
        detail={"steps_completed": auto_completed},
    )
```

---

### 7. **Two Resolution Paths**

**Path A: Synthetic Issues** (triage::*, workflow::*, subjective::*)
- Handled in `cmd_plan_resolve` itself (lines 534-700)
- Calls `purge_ids(plan, synthetic_ids)` directly
- Appends "done" log entry

**Path B: Real Issues**
- Delegated to `cmd_resolve` (imported from `app/commands/resolve/cmd.py`)
- `cmd_resolve` resolves in state (JSON), then calls back to `_update_living_plan_after_resolve`
- This is where cluster context is captured and "resolve" log entry is appended

**For auto-step-completion:** You need hooks in BOTH paths:
1. After synthetic ID `purge_ids()` in `cmd_plan_resolve`
2. In `_update_living_plan_after_resolve` after real issue `purge_ids()`

---

### 8. **Data Available at Integration Point**

At the moment of auto-completion, you have:
- `plan`: Full plan object with all clusters and steps
- `all_resolved`: List of issue IDs just resolved
- `args.status`: "fixed", "open", etc. (only auto-complete on "fixed"?)
- Cluster membership via `overrides`

---

| Command handler | `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/override_handlers.py` |
| Resolve integration (real issues) | `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/resolve/cmd.py` |

## Context

## Improvements to implement

**Current:** `queue_render.py:_render_cluster_banner()` and `_cluster_type_label()` don't distinguish manual clusters.

**Current:** `guardrails.py:print_triage_guardrail_info()` always prints.
**Fix:** Add `output_format` parameter, return warning text instead of printing for non-terminal. Add context: "since last triage. Run `desloppify plan triage` to incorporate."

### 7. Show step progress in cluster cards
**Current:** No step progress shown.
**Fix:** In `render_cluster_item()` and `_render_cluster_banner()`, when steps exist, count done steps and show `[2/7 steps done]`.

### 8. Explain queue numbering gaps
**Current:** Cluster banners consume positions but table rows skip them.
**Fix:** After the table in `cmd_plan_queue`, if clusters were rendered as banners, add note explaining the gap.

### 9. Trim encouragement box
**Current:** `cmd.py:_build_and_render_queue()` lines 328-338 — 8 lines.

**Current:** No hint about how to mark steps done.
**Fix:** In cluster drill-in view header (render.py), add hint: `Mark step done: desloppify plan cluster update <name> --done-step N`

### 11. Auto-complete steps on resolve (KEY FEATURE)
**Current:** Steps must be manually marked done.
**Fix:** In resolve flow (`app/commands/resolve/cmd.py:_update_living_plan_after_resolve` and `app/commands/plan/override_handlers.py:cmd_plan_resolve`), after `purge_ids()`, check all clusters' steps. If a step's `issue_refs` are all no longer in the queue, mark `done=True`.

Schema already supports this: `ActionStep` has `issue_refs: list[str]` and `done: bool`.

Two resolution paths need the hook:
- Path A: Synthetic issues in `override_handlers.py:cmd_plan_resolve` (after `purge_ids` on line ~534-700)
- Path B: Real issues in `resolve/cmd.py:_update_living_plan_after_resolve` (after `purge_ids` on line ~110)

Algorithm (put in `engine/_plan/` as a shared function):
```python
def auto_complete_steps(plan: dict, resolved_ids: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Mark steps done when all issue_refs are resolved. Returns messages."""
    messages = []
    queue_set = set(plan.get("queue_order", []))
    for name, cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items():
        for i, step in enumerate(cluster.get("action_steps") or []):
            if not isinstance(step, dict) or step.get("done"):
                continue
            refs = step.get("issue_refs", [])
            if not refs:
                continue
            # Match by suffix: ref "abc123" matches "review::path::abc123"
            all_resolved = all(
                not any(qid.endswith(ref) for qid in queue_set)
                for ref in refs
            )
            if all_resolved:
                step["done"] = True
                messages.append(f"Step {i+1} of '{name}' auto-completed: {step.get('title', '')}")
    return messages
```

### 12. Surface dependency_order
**Current:** `dependency_order` exists on Cluster schema but never displayed.
**Fix:** In `cluster show` and `cluster list --verbose`, show dependency_order if set. In `next` cluster card, note if cluster should be done before others.

- `engine/_plan/step_parser.py` — step parsing/formatting utilities

## Constraints
- Don't break existing tests
- Minimize scope of each change
- Reuse existing infrastructure (ActionStep schema, step_parser utilities)
- The auto-complete-steps function should be in engine/_plan/ since it's plan logic, not command logic

    48→class NextOptions:
    49→    """All user-facing options for the ``next`` command, extracted once."""
    50→

    61→    @classmethod

    63→        """Build from an argparse Namespace, applying defaults for missing attrs."""
    64→        return cls(

    66→            scope=getattr(args, "scope", None),

    84→
    85→def _low_subjective_dimensions(
    86→    state: dict,
    87→    dim_scores: dict,
    88→    *,
    89→    threshold: float = DEFAULT_TARGET_STRICT_SCORE,
    90→) -> list[tuple[str, float, int]]:
    91→    """Return assessed scorecard-subjective entries below the threshold."""
    92→    low: list[tuple[str, float, int]] = []
    93→    for entry in _scorecard_subjective(state, dim_scores):
    94→        if entry.get("placeholder"):
    95→            continue
    96→        strict_val = float(entry.get("strict", entry.get("score", 100.0)))
    97→        if strict_val < threshold:
    98→            low.append(
    99→                (
   100→                    str(entry.get("name", "Subjective")),
   101→                    strict_val,
   102→                    int(entry.get("failing", 0)),
   103→                )
   104→            )
   105→    low.sort(key=lambda item: item[1])
   106→    return low

   108→
   109→def cmd_next(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   110→    """Show next highest-priority queue items."""
   111→    runtime = command_runtime(args)
   112→    state = runtime.state
   113→    config = runtime.config
   114→    if not require_completed_scan(state):
   115→        return
   116→
   117→    skill_warning = check_skill_version()
   118→    if skill_warning:
   119→        print(colorize(f"  {skill_warning}", "yellow"))
   120→    config_warning = check_config_staleness(config)
   121→    if config_warning:
   122→        print(colorize(f"  {config_warning}", "yellow"))
   123→
   124→    print_triage_guardrail_info(state=state)
   125→    _build_and_render_queue(args, state, config)
   126→
   127→
   128→def _resolve_cluster_focus(
   129→    plan_data: dict | None,
   130→    *,
   131→    cluster_arg: str | None,
   132→    scope: str | None,
   133→) -> str | None:
   134→    effective_cluster = cluster_arg
   135→    if plan_data and not cluster_arg and not scope:
   136→        active_cluster = plan_data.get("active_cluster")
   137→        if active_cluster:
   138→            effective_cluster = active_cluster
   139→    return effective_cluster
   140→

   142→def _build_next_payload(
   143→    *,
   144→    queue: dict,
   145→    items: list[dict],
   146→    state: dict,
   147→    narrative: dict,
   148→    plan_data: dict | None,
   149→) -> dict:
   150→    payload = next_output_mod.build_query_payload(
   151→        queue, items, command="next", narrative=narrative, plan=plan_data
   152→    )
   153→    scores = state_mod.score_snapshot(state)
   154→    payload["overall_score"] = scores.overall
   155→    payload["objective_score"] = scores.objective
   156→    payload["strict_score"] = scores.strict
   157→    payload["scorecard_dimensions"] = scorecard_dimensions_payload(
   158→        state,
   159→        dim_scores=state.get("dimension_scores", {}),
   160→    )
   161→    payload["subjective_measures"] = [
   162→        row for row in payload["scorecard_dimensions"] if row.get("subjective")
   163→    ]
   164→    return payload
   165→

   167→def _emit_requested_output(
   168→    opts: NextOptions,
   169→    payload: dict,
   170→    items: list[dict],
   171→) -> bool:
   172→    if opts.output_file:
   173→        if next_output_mod.write_output_file(
   174→            opts.output_file,
   175→            payload,
   176→            len(items),
   177→            safe_write_text_fn=safe_write_text,
   178→            colorize_fn=colorize,
   179→        ):
   180→            return True
   181→        raise CommandError("Failed to write output file")
   182→
   183→    if next_output_mod.emit_non_terminal_output(opts.output_format, payload, items):
   184→        return True
   185→    return False

   188→def _plan_queue_context(
   189→    *,
   190→    state: dict,
   191→    plan_data: dict | None,
   192→    context=None,
   193→) -> tuple[float | None, QueueBreakdown | None]:
   194→    effective_plan = context.plan if context is not None else plan_data
   195→    plan_start_strict = get_plan_start_strict(effective_plan)
   196→    try:
   197→        breakdown = plan_aware_queue_breakdown(state, plan_data, context=context)
   198→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS:
   199→        breakdown = None
   200→    return plan_start_strict, breakdown

   203→def _merge_potentials_safe(raw_potentials: dict | None) -> dict | None:
   204→    try:
   205→        return merge_potentials(raw_potentials) or None
   206→    except (ImportError, TypeError, ValueError):
   207→        return raw_potentials or None
